snapshot.stmt: There are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, for every sufficiently small \(h\), the perturbations generated by \(b_h\) yield two observed-data laws \(\mathbb P_{+,h},\mathbb P_{-,h}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) whose source marginals satisfy \[\operatorname{KL}(P_{+,h}^{S,n},P_{-,h}^{S,n})\le Cnh^{2s+a+1},\qquad |\tau(\mathbb P_{+,h})-\tau(\mathbb P_{-,h})|\ge ch^{s+1}.\] A separate smooth target-density perturbation yields two full-data laws whose observed target projections have divergence bounded by a constant and target separation at least \(cm^{-1/2}\).

snapshot.stmt: For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), the deterministic choices \(h=h_n\) and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\) give \[\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_n}-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2}\le C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] Uniformly over the same sequence, the fold-trained dual extensions evaluated on their held-out source folds obey \[\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}=O_P\!\left(1+\log(1/h_n)\mathbf 1\{a=1\}+h_n^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{a>1\}\right),\] \[\frac{\max_i\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2}{\sum_i\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2}=o_P(1),\qquad \sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h_n,J_n}(v)|=O_P\{\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] The threshold \(t>1/2\) controls approximation of the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, whereas the product relation controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. These out-of-sample stability and residual bounds are conclusions derived from the primal program, its normalized dual extension, spline geometry, and primitive density conditions, not model assumptions.

defs.def:model-class: \[\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\bigl\{\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}:\exists(F^S_{n,m},F^T_{n,m})\text{ with }P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m},\ P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m},\text{ and every listed member-property assumption holds at the fixed indices }(n,m,a,s,t)\bigr\}.\] The finite-\((n,m)\) class contains no condition on how \(m/n\) behaves along a sequence.
defs.def:ricot-weights: For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy the nonredundant calibration equations \(\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\). If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of \[\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).\] Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus \(\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2\). Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the out-of-sample extension \[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.\] This formula is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J,1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\): it agrees with that density at every source training atom and is a positive measurable function at independent held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\).
defs.def:spliced-estimator: Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define \[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.\] Thus each displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), so the residual correction is not an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\).
defs.def:regression-fit: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set \[\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},\qquad \widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.\] Regress \(Z\) on \(\mathbf b_{h,J}\) using the same training indices with \(X\ge h\), the normalized least-squares objective, and ridge \(n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2\). Define \(\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(x)\) as \(\max\{-1,\min\{1,\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}\}\) for \(x<h\) and as the analogously truncated fitted spline for \(x\ge h\). Define \(\widehat d_{k,h}(x)=\mathbf 1\{|\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}|<1\}\), taking value zero at equality. Empty local samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridge, ordered basis, and stated kink convention make every fold fit and its boundary linearization unique.

snapshot.stmt: Under \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), in the special case \(a=0\), \(r(x)=g_T(x)/g_S(x)\) is uniformly bounded, \(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), and \[h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2},\qquad \int_{h_n}^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx=O(1).\] The dual extension in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\) is strictly positive on every held-out \(x\in[h_n,1]\) whenever both training interior measures are nonzero, so the residual correction in \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_n}\) does not collapse to zero. snapshot.stmt: For fixed \((a,s,t,M)\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence satisfying \(m/n\to\kappa\), the interval \(\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\) obeys \[\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\}\ge1-\gamma,\] and its maximal expected length is at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\). The resulting studentized linear term has Kolmogorov distance \(o(1)\) from \(N(0,1)\), and conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) the law of \(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h_n,J_n}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h_n,J_n}|\) approximates its centered sampling analogue with error \(o(1)\). The conclusion includes \(a=1\), where the normal approximation is scaled by \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and the \(2M\) boundary-bias envelope remains explicit.

No unreported fitted quantity or prose-specified variance component enters the interval.

defs.def:foldwise-inference-statistics: For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define the held-out target and interior-residual summands \[\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}=\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_j^T),\qquad \widehat U^R_{i,h,J}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.\] The source-side linear effect of estimating the boundary polynomial in every fold whose training set contains source observation \(i\) is \[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\widehat d_{k,h}(X_j^T)\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.\] Thus \(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}\) is exactly the displayed first-order boundary local-polynomial training contribution to the target plug-in average, with the truncation derivative fixed by \(\widehat d_{k,h}\). defs.def:calibration-residual-envelope: Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make \(\{\zeta_i^S:i=1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{\zeta_j^T:j=1,\ldots,m\}\) mutually independent standard-normal variables. snapshot.stmt: The multiscale handle in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\) does not, as presently constructed, define a single interval-valued statistic. It specifies neither measurable exponent estimators, thresholds, a selection rule, nor tie breaking. Consequently the frozen construction has no coverage probability or expected length to evaluate and does not yield the proposed adaptive guarantee. A positive result requires a new executable construction before self-similarity can be used to prove adaptation.

defs.def:adaptive-handle: Use dyadic differences of adjacent boundary local-polynomial fits to estimate persistent boundary approximation error, estimate \(a\) from source empirical masses of dyadic boundary shells, and combine these diagnostics with interior Riesz-calibration residuals to select one pair from \(\{\mathcal I_{h,J}:h\text{ dyadic},\ J=\lceil h^{-1}\rceil\}\).
defs.def:bias-aware-interval: Using only the statistics displayed in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), and \(\mathrm{def:calibration\text{-}residual\text{-}envelope}\), define \[\mathcal I_{h,J}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}\pm\operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}\!\left(\frac{\widehat B_{h,J}+\widehat E_{h,J}}{\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}}\right)\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}\right].\] If \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}=0\), define \(\mathcal I_{h,J}=\mathbb R\) when \(\widehat B_{h,J}+\widehat E_{h,J}>0\), and define the singleton \(\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}\}\) otherwise. snapshot.stmt: For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), the deterministic choices \(h=h_n\) and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\) give \[\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_n}-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2}\le C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] Uniformly over the same sequence, the fold-trained dual extensions evaluated on their held-out source folds obey \[\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}=O_P\!\left(1+\log(1/h_n)\mathbf 1\{a=1\}+h_n^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{a>1\}\right),\] \[\frac{\max_i\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2}{\sum_i\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2}=o_P(1),\qquad \sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h_n,J_n}(v)|=O_P\{\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] The threshold \(t>1/2\) controls approximation of the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, whereas the product relation controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. assumptions.ass:mean-transportability: \(\mathbb E_{F^T_{n,m}}[Y^T(d)\mid X^T=x]=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}[Y^S(d)\mid X=x]=\mu_d(x)\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).

snapshot.stmt: Under \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), in the special case \(a=0\), \(r(x)=g_T(x)/g_S(x)\) is uniformly bounded, \(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), and \[h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2},\qquad \int_{h_n}^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx=O(1).\] The dual extension in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\) is strictly positive on every held-out \(x\in[h_n,1]\) whenever both training interior measures are nonzero, so the residual correction in \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_n}\) does not collapse to zero. Consequently its boundary bias, source stochastic term, and target empirical term are respectively \(O(n^{-1/2})\), \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\), and \(O_P(m^{-1/2})\), giving the ordinary two-sample root-risk reduction \(O(m^{-1/2}+n^{-1/2})\).

defs.def:ricot-weights: For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy the nonredundant calibration equations \(\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\). If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of \[\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).\] Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus \(\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2\). Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the out-of-sample extension \[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.\] This formula is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J,1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\): it agrees with that density at every source training atom and is a positive measurable function at independent held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\).
defs.def:spliced-estimator: Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define \[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.\] Thus each displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), so the residual correction is not an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\).
defs.def:regression-fit: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set \[\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},\qquad \widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.\] Regress \(Z\) on \(\mathbf b_{h,J}\) using the same training indices with \(X\ge h\), the normalized least-squares objective, and ridge \(n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2\). Define \(\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(x)\) as \(\max\{-1,\min\{1,\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}\}\) for \(x<h\) and as the analogously truncated fitted spline for \(x\ge h\). Define \(\widehat d_{k,h}(x)=\mathbf 1\{|\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}|<1\}\), taking value zero at equality. Empty local samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridge, ordered basis, and stated kink convention make every fold fit and its boundary linearization unique.

snapshot.stmt: For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), combining the preceding bounds gives \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\asymp m^{-1/2}+\begin{cases}n^{-1/2},&a<1,\\ \sqrt{\log n/n},&a=1,\\ n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)},&a>1.\end{cases}\] At \(a=0\), \(\mathrm{prop:a0\text{-}sanity\text{-}reduction}\) gives the bounded-ratio ordinary two-sample root rate directly for this covariate-only target model. Within the same model, \(0<a<1\) permits an unbounded but square-integrable Riesz weight without losing that root rate; \(a=1\) and \(a>1\) give its critical and nonregular continuations.

assumptions.ass:mean-transportability: \(\mathbb E_{F^T_{n,m}}[Y^T(d)\mid X^T=x]=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}[Y^S(d)\mid X=x]=\mu_d(x)\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).

snapshot.stmt: For fixed \((a,s,t,M)\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence satisfying \(m/n\to\kappa\), the interval \(\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\) obeys \[\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\}\ge1-\gamma,\] and its maximal expected length is at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\). Uniformly over the class, the explicit four-term statistic \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h_n,J_n}^2\) in \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), including the covariance between \(\widehat U^R_{i,h_n,J_n}\) and \(\widehat U^B_{i,h_n,J_n}\), divided by the variance of the corresponding foldwise linear term converges in probability to one. The resulting studentized linear term has Kolmogorov distance \(o(1)\) from \(N(0,1)\), and conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) the law of \(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h_n,J_n}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h_n,J_n}|\) approximates its centered sampling analogue with error \(o(1)\). The threshold \(t>1/2\) controls the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, while the product relation controls the separate nuisance-product remainder. These approximations are derived from the product experiment \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\), bounded outcomes, the optimizer leverage bound in \(\mathrm{thm:ricot\text{-}attainment}\), and the entropy of the one-dimensional Hölder ball after spline-calibration projection. The conclusion includes \(a=1\), where the normal approximation is scaled by \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and the \(2M\) boundary-bias envelope remains explicit.

defs.def:bias-aware-interval: Using only the statistics displayed in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), and \(\mathrm{def:calibration\text{-}residual\text{-}envelope}\), define \[\mathcal I_{h,J}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}\pm\operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}\!\left(\frac{\widehat B_{h,J}+\widehat E_{h,J}}{\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}}\right)\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}\right].\] If \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}=0\), define \(\mathcal I_{h,J}=\mathbb R\) when \(\widehat B_{h,J}+\widehat E_{h,J}>0\), and define the singleton \(\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}\}\) otherwise. No unreported fitted quantity or prose-specified variance component enters the interval.

defs.def:bias-envelope: \[\widehat B_{h,J}=2C_{\mathrm{LP}}Mh^{s+1}+2M\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h,J}(v)|.\] The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\) from the two armwise radius-\(M\) balls, and the displayed support function is indexed by \(J\) through the fitted transport weight inside \(\Delta_{h,J}\).
defs.def:foldwise-inference-statistics: For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define the held-out target and interior-residual summands \[\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}=\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_j^T),\qquad \widehat U^R_{i,h,J}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.\] The source-side linear effect of estimating the boundary polynomial in every fold whose training set contains source observation \(i\) is \[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\widehat d_{k,h}(X_j^T)\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.\] Thus \(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}\) is exactly the displayed first-order boundary local-polynomial training contribution to the target plug-in average, with the truncation derivative fixed by \(\widehat d_{k,h}\). For any fold-indexed numbers \((W_u)\), write \(\overline W_k^S=(N_k^S)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}W_i\) and \(\overline W_k^T=(N_k^T)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}W_j\). Define the fully observable standard error by \[\begin{aligned}\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}^2={}&\frac1{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^T}{N_k^T-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}(\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^T}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac2{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J}).\end{aligned}\] The four lines are respectively the target variance, interior source variance, boundary source variance, and their within-source covariance. There is no primitive source--target covariance because \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\) is the product experiment; randomness of fold-trained coefficients is retained in every displayed summand and its asymptotic remainder is controlled in the honesty theorem. A term with fold size at most one is defined to be zero.
defs.def:calibration-residual-envelope: Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make \(\{\zeta_i^S:i=1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{\zeta_j^T:j=1,\ldots,m\}\) mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define the fold-centered calibration process \[\begin{aligned}\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].\end{aligned}\] Define the boundary contribution, using the exact local-polynomial linear summand from \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), by \[\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J}\right].\] The computable random envelope is \[\widehat E_{h,J}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.\] Empty-fold averages are zero; with the deterministic modulo allocation they are absent once \(n,m\ge K_0\). The same source multipliers appear in both source pieces, so their covariance is retained, while all target multipliers are independent of all source multipliers.

assumptions.ass:residual-nondegeneracy: \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)\ge M^{-1}\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_S\)-almost every \(x\).

snapshot.stmt: The multiscale handle in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\) does not, as presently constructed, define a single interval-valued statistic. It specifies neither measurable exponent estimators, thresholds, a selection rule, nor tie breaking. Consequently the frozen construction has no coverage probability or expected length to evaluate and does not yield the proposed adaptive guarantee. A positive result requires a new executable construction before self-similarity can be used to prove adaptation.

defs.def:adaptive-handle: Use dyadic differences of adjacent boundary local-polynomial fits to estimate persistent boundary approximation error, estimate \(a\) from source empirical masses of dyadic boundary shells, and combine these diagnostics with interior Riesz-calibration residuals to select one pair from \(\{\mathcal I_{h,J}:h\text{ dyadic},\ J=\lceil h^{-1}\rceil\}\).

No unreported fitted quantity or prose-specified variance component enters the interval.

If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\).
defs.def:bias-envelope: \[\widehat B_{h,J}=2C_{\mathrm{LP}}Mh^{s+1}+2M\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h,J}(v)|.\] The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\) from the two armwise radius-\(M\) balls, and the displayed support function is indexed by \(J\) through the fitted transport weight inside \(\Delta_{h,J}\).
defs.def:foldwise-inference-statistics: For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define the held-out target and interior-residual summands \[\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}=\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_j^T),\qquad \widehat U^R_{i,h,J}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.\] The source-side linear effect of estimating the boundary polynomial in every fold whose training set contains source observation \(i\) is \[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\widehat d_{k,h}(X_j^T)\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.\] Thus \(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}\) is exactly the displayed first-order boundary local-polynomial training contribution to the target plug-in average, with the truncation derivative fixed by \(\widehat d_{k,h}\). For any fold-indexed numbers \((W_u)\), write \(\overline W_k^S=(N_k^S)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}W_i\) and \(\overline W_k^T=(N_k^T)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}W_j\). Define the fully observable standard error by \[\begin{aligned}\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}^2={}&\frac1{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^T}{N_k^T-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}(\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^T}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac2{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J}).\end{aligned}\] The four lines are respectively the target variance, interior source variance, boundary source variance, and their within-source covariance. There is no primitive source--target covariance because \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\) is the product experiment; randomness of fold-trained coefficients is retained in every displayed summand and its asymptotic remainder is controlled in the honesty theorem. A term with fold size at most one is defined to be zero.
defs.def:calibration-residual-envelope: Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make \(\{\zeta_i^S:i=1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{\zeta_j^T:j=1,\ldots,m\}\) mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define the fold-centered calibration process \[\begin{aligned}\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].\end{aligned}\] Define the boundary contribution, using the exact local-polynomial linear summand from \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), by \[\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J}\right].\] The computable random envelope is \[\widehat E_{h,J}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.\] Empty-fold averages are zero; with the deterministic modulo allocation they are absent once \(n,m\ge K_0\). The same source multipliers appear in both source pieces, so their covariance is retained, while all target multipliers are independent of all source multipliers.

assumptions.ass:boundary-self-similarity: \(c_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\le\inf_{q\in\mathcal P_p}\sup_{x\in[h/2,h]}|\mu(x)-q(x)|\le C_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\) for every dyadic \(h\le h_0\).

snapshot.stmt: For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), the deterministic choices \(h=h_n\) and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\) give \[\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_n}-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2}\le C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] Uniformly over the same sequence, the fold-trained dual extensions evaluated on their held-out source folds obey \[\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}=O_P\!\left(1+\log(1/h_n)\mathbf 1\{a=1\}+h_n^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{a>1\}\right),\] \[\frac{\max_i\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2}{\sum_i\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_n}(X_i)\}^2}=o_P(1).\] The threshold \(t>1/2\) controls approximation of the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, whereas the product relation controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. These out-of-sample stability bounds are conclusions derived from the primal program, its normalized dual extension, spline geometry, and primitive density conditions, not model assumptions.

defs.def:model-class: \[\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\bigl\{\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}:\exists(F^S_{n,m},F^T_{n,m})\text{ with }P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m},\ P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m},\text{ and every listed member-property assumption holds at the fixed indices }(n,m,a,s,t)\bigr\}.\] The finite-\((n,m)\) class contains no condition on how \(m/n\) behaves along a sequence.
defs.def:ricot-weights: For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy the nonredundant calibration equations \(\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\). If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of \[\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).\] Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus \(\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2\). Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the out-of-sample extension \[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.\] This formula is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J,1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\): it agrees with that density at every source training atom and is a positive measurable function at independent held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\).
defs.def:spliced-estimator: Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define \[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.\] Thus each displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), so the residual correction is not an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\).
defs.def:regression-fit: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set \[\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},\qquad \widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.\] Regress \(Z\) on \(\mathbf b_{h,J}\) using the same training indices with \(X\ge h\), the normalized least-squares objective, and ridge \(n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2\). Define \(\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(x)\) as \(\max\{-1,\min\{1,\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}\}\) for \(x<h\) and as the analogously truncated fitted spline for \(x\ge h\). Define \(\widehat d_{k,h}(x)=\mathbf 1\{|\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}|<1\}\), taking value zero at equality. Empty local samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridge, ordered basis, and stated kink convention make every fold fit and its boundary linearization unique.

assumptions.ass:known-propensity: \(e\) is fixed and known by the source-trial randomization protocol.
assumptions.ass:mean-transportability: \(\mathbb E_{F^T_{n,m}}[Y^T(d)\mid X^T=x]=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}[Y^S(d)\mid X=x]=\mu_d(x)\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).

snapshot.stmt: Under \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), in the special case \(a=0\), \(r(x)=g_T(x)/g_S(x)\) is uniformly bounded, \(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), and \[h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2},\qquad \int_{h_n}^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx=O(1).\] The dual extension in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\) is strictly positive on every held-out \(x\in[h_n,1]\) whenever both training interior measures are nonzero, so the residual correction in \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_n}\) does not collapse to zero. snapshot.stmt: For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), combining the preceding bounds gives \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\asymp m^{-1/2}+\begin{cases}n^{-1/2},&a<1,\\ \sqrt{\log n/n},&a=1,\\ n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)},&a>1.\end{cases}\] At \(a=0\), \(\mathrm{prop:a0\text{-}sanity\text{-}reduction}\) gives the bounded-ratio ordinary two-sample root rate directly for this covariate-only target model. snapshot.stmt: For fixed \((a,s,t,M)\) with \(s>1/2\), \(t>1/2\), and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence satisfying \(m/n\to\kappa\), the interval \(\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\), with the finite zero-standard-error convention in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\), obeys \[\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\}\ge1-\gamma,\] and its maximal expected length is at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\). Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy the nonredundant calibration equations \(\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\). If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of \[\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).\] Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus \(\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2\). Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. defs.def:bias-envelope: \[\widehat B_{h,J}=2C_{\mathrm{LP}}Mh^{s+1}+2M\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h,J}(v)|.\] The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\) from the two armwise radius-\(M\) balls, and the displayed support function is indexed by \(J\) through the fitted transport weight inside \(\Delta_{h,J}\).
defs.def:foldwise-inference-statistics: For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define the held-out target and interior-residual summands \[\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}=\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_j^T),\qquad \widehat U^R_{i,h,J}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.\] The source-side linear effect of estimating the boundary polynomial in every fold whose training set contains source observation \(i\) is \[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\widehat d_{k,h}(X_j^T)\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.\] Thus \(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}\) is exactly the displayed first-order boundary local-polynomial training contribution to the target plug-in average, with the truncation derivative fixed by \(\widehat d_{k,h}\). For any fold-indexed numbers \((W_u)\), write \(\overline W_k^S=(N_k^S)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}W_i\) and \(\overline W_k^T=(N_k^T)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}W_j\). Define the fully observable standard error by \[\begin{aligned}\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}^2={}&\frac1{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^T}{N_k^T-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}(\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^T}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac2{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J}).\end{aligned}\] The four lines are respectively the target variance, interior source variance, boundary source variance, and their within-source covariance. A term with fold size at most one is defined to be zero.
defs.def:calibration-residual-envelope: Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make \(\{\zeta_i^S:i=1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{\zeta_j^T:j=1,\ldots,m\}\) mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define the fold-centered calibration process \[\begin{aligned}\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].\end{aligned}\] Define the boundary contribution, using the exact local-polynomial linear summand from \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), by \[\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J}\right].\] The computable random envelope is \[\widehat E_{h,J}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.\] Empty-fold averages are zero; with the deterministic modulo allocation they are absent once \(n,m\ge K_0\). \[
\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2}\le C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.
\]
Uniformly over the same sequence, the fold-trained dual extensions evaluated on their held-out source folds obey
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}=O_P\!\left(1+\log(1/h_n)\mathbf 1\{a=1\}+h_n^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{a>1\}\right)
\]
and
\[

\]
with the ratio defined as zero when the denominator is zero. The threshold \(t>1/2\) controls approximation of the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, whereas the product relation controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. These out-of-sample stability bounds are conclusions to be derived from the primal program, normalized dual extension, spline geometry, and primitive density conditions, not model assumptions.

defs.def:spliced-estimator:
Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define

+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.
\]
Every displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), not as an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\). defs.def:regression-fit:
For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set
\[

\qquad

\]
Using the same training indices with \(X_i\ge h\), let \(\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}\) be the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{J_{\mu,n}}\) of
\[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_i)^\top\beta\}^2+n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2.
\]

\[

\begin{cases}
\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h},&0\le x<h,\\
\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)^\top\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}},&h\le x\le1.
\end{cases}
\]

snapshot.stmt:
For fixed \((a,s,t,M)\) with \(s>1/2\), \(t>1/2\), and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence satisfying \(m/n\to\kappa\), the interval \(\mathcal I_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), with the finite zero-standard-error convention in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\), obeys
\[
\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\}\ge1-\gamma,
\]
and its maximal expected length is at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\). Uniformly over the class, the explicit four-term statistic \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}^2\), including the covariance between \(\widehat U^R_{i,h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat U^B_{i,h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), divided by the variance of the corresponding foldwise linear term converges in probability to one. The studentized linear term has Kolmogorov distance \(o(1)\) from \(N(0,1)\), and conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) the law of
\[
\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}|
\]
approximates its centered sampling analogue with error \(o(1)\). The threshold \(s>1/2\) gives the finite one-dimensional Hölder entropy integral, \(t>1/2\) controls the density-ratio calibration sieve, and the product relation controls the nuisance-product remainder. The conclusion includes \(a=1\), where the normal approximation is scaled by \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and the \(2M\) boundary-bias envelope remains explicit.

defs.def:bias-aware-interval:
Using only the displayed bias, multiplier-envelope, and standard-error statistics, define, when \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}>0\),
\[
\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\pm\operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}\!\left(\frac{\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}}{\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}}\right)\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right].
\]
If \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=0\), define
\[
\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-(\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}),\ \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+(\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})\right].
\]
This is the finite continuous extension of the bias-aware radius and is a singleton if both envelopes vanish.
defs.def:spliced-estimator:
Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=
\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)
+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.
\]
Every displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), not as an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\). The regression and calibration dimensions are respectively \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\); only \(h\) is the boundary-splice bandwidth.
defs.def:regression-fit:
For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set
\[
\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},
\qquad
\widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.
\]
Using the same training indices with \(X_i\ge h\), let \(\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}\) be the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{J_{\mu,n}}\) of
\[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_i)^\top\beta\}^2+n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2.
\]
Define the untruncated fit
\[
\widehat\mu^{(-k)}_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h},&0\le x<h,\\
\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)^\top\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}},&h\le x\le1.
\end{cases}
\]
Empty local or interior samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridges and ordered bases make every fold fit unique. No clipping map or kink derivative is part of the construction.
defs.def:ricot-weights:
For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.
\]
This is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), agrees with that density at source training atoms, and is positive and measurable at held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.
defs.def:bias-envelope:
\[
\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=2C_{\mathrm{LP}}Mh^{s+1}+2M\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)|.
\]
The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\) from the two armwise radius-\(M\) balls. The regression dimension is displayed because the interval is attached to \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), while the calibration support function itself depends on \(J_{r,n}\) through its fitted transport weight.
defs.def:foldwise-inference-statistics:
For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define
\[
\widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_j^T),
\qquad
\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.
\]
Because the boundary fit is untruncated, its ordinary ridge/local-polynomial linear summand is
\[
\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.
\]
For fold-indexed numbers \((W_u)\), write \(\overline W_k^S=(N_k^S)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}W_i\) and \(\overline W_k^T=(N_k^T)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}W_j\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}^2={}&\frac1{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^T}{N_k^T-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}(\widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^T}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac2{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The four lines are the target variance, interior source variance, boundary source variance, and within-source covariance. There is no primitive source--target covariance because \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\). A term with fold size at most one is zero.
defs.def:calibration-residual-envelope:
Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make the source and target multipliers mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\
&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Define
\[
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right]
\]
and
\[
\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.
\]
Empty-fold averages are zero. The same source multipliers appear in both source pieces, retaining their covariance, and all target multipliers are independent of all source multipliers.

assumptions.ass:residual-nondegeneracy: \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)\ge M^{-1}\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_S\)-almost every \(x\).

snapshot.stmt: The multiscale handle in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\) does not, as presently constructed, define a single interval-valued statistic. It specifies neither measurable exponent estimators, thresholds, a selection rule, nor tie breaking. Consequently the frozen construction has no coverage probability or expected length to evaluate and does not yield the proposed adaptive guarantee. A positive result requires a new executable construction before self-similarity can be used to prove adaptation.

defs.def:adaptive-handle: Use dyadic differences of adjacent untruncated boundary local-polynomial fits to estimate persistent boundary approximation error, estimate \(a\) from source empirical masses of dyadic boundary shells, and combine these diagnostics with interior Riesz-calibration residuals to select one interval from \(\{\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}:h\text{ dyadic}\}\). The handle still does not specify the measurable exponent estimators, thresholds, selection rule, or tie breaking.

Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make the source and target multipliers mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\
&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Define
\[
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right]
\]
and
\[
\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.
\]
Empty-fold averages are zero. The same source multipliers appear in both source pieces, retaining their covariance, and all target multipliers are independent of all source multipliers.

assumptions.ass:boundary-self-similarity: \(c_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\le\inf_{q\in\mathcal P_p}\sup_{x\in[h/2,h]}|\mu(x)-q(x)|\le C_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\) for every dyadic \(h\le h_0\).

For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), the deterministic choices \(h=h_n\), \(J_\mu=J_{\mu,n}\), and \(J_r=J_{r,n}\) give
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2}\le C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.
\]
Uniformly over the same sequence, the fold-trained dual extensions evaluated on their held-out source folds obey
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}=O_P\!\left(1+\log(1/h_n)\mathbf 1\{a=1\}+h_n^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{a>1\}\right)
\]
and
\[
\frac{\max_{i:X_i\ge h_n}\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}}=o_P(1),

defs.def:model-class: \[\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\bigl\{\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}:\exists(F^S_{n,m},F^T_{n,m})\text{ with }P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m},\ P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m},\text{ and every listed member-property assumption holds at the fixed indices }(n,m,a,s,t)\bigr\}.\] The finite-\((n,m)\) class contains no condition on how \(m/n\) behaves along a sequence.
defs.def:ricot-weights:
For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.
\]
This is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), agrees with that density at source training atoms, and is positive and measurable at held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.
defs.def:spliced-estimator:
Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=
\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)
+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.
\]
Every displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), not as an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\). The regression and calibration dimensions are respectively \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\); only \(h\) is the boundary-splice bandwidth.
defs.def:regression-fit:
For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set
\[
\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},
\qquad
\widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.
\]
Using the same training indices with \(X_i\ge h\), let \(\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}\) be the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{J_{\mu,n}}\) of
\[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_i)^\top\beta\}^2+n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2.
\]
Define the untruncated fit
\[
\widehat\mu^{(-k)}_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h},&0\le x<h,\\
\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)^\top\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}},&h\le x\le1.
\end{cases}
\]
Empty local or interior samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridges and ordered bases make every fold fit unique. No clipping map or kink derivative is part of the construction.

assumptions.ass:mean-transportability: \(\mathbb E_{F^T_{n,m}}[Y^T(d)\mid X^T=x]=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}[Y^S(d)\mid X=x]=\mu_d(x)\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).

\[
\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\}\ge1-\gamma,
\]

The studentized linear term has Kolmogorov distance \(o(1)\) from \(N(0,1)\), and conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) the law of
\[
\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}|
\]

defs.def:bias-aware-interval:

\]

\[
\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-(\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}),\ \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+(\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})\right].

The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\) from the two armwise radius-\(M\) balls. The regression dimension is displayed because the interval is attached to \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), while the calibration support function itself depends on \(J_{r,n}\) through its fitted transport weight.
defs.def:foldwise-inference-statistics:
For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define
\[
\widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_j^T),
\qquad
\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.
\]
Because the boundary fit is untruncated, its ordinary ridge/local-polynomial linear summand is
\[
\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.
\]
For fold-indexed numbers \((W_u)\), write \(\overline W_k^S=(N_k^S)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}W_i\) and \(\overline W_k^T=(N_k^T)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}W_j\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}^2={}&\frac1{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^T}{N_k^T-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}(\widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^T}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac2{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The four lines are the target variance, interior source variance, boundary source variance, and within-source covariance. There is no primitive source--target covariance because \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\). A term with fold size at most one is zero.
defs.def:calibration-residual-envelope:
Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make the source and target multipliers mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\
&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Define
\[
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right]
\]
and
\[
\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.
\]
Empty-fold averages are zero. The same source multipliers appear in both source pieces, retaining their covariance, and all target multipliers are independent of all source multipliers.

assumptions.ass:residual-nondegeneracy: \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)\ge M^{-1}\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_S\)-almost every \(x\).

snapshot.stmt:
For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), the deterministic choices \(h=h_n\), \(J_\mu=J_{\mu,n}\), and \(J_r=J_{r,n}\) give
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2}\le C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.
\]
Uniformly over the same sequence, the fold-trained dual extensions evaluated on their held-out source folds obey
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}=O_P\!\left(1+\log(1/h_n)\mathbf 1\{a=1\}+h_n^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{a>1\}\right)
\]
and
\[
\frac{\max_{i:X_i\ge h_n}\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}}=o_P(1),
\]
with the ratio defined as zero when the denominator is zero. The threshold \(t>1/2\) controls approximation of the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, whereas the product relation controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. These out-of-sample stability bounds are conclusions to be derived from the primal program, normalized dual extension, spline geometry, and primitive density conditions, not model assumptions.

defs.def:model-class: \[\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\bigl\{\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}:\exists(F^S_{n,m},F^T_{n,m})\text{ with }P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m},\ P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m},\text{ and every listed member-property assumption holds at the fixed indices }(n,m,a,s,t)\bigr\}.\] The finite-\((n,m)\) class contains no condition on how \(m/n\) behaves along a sequence.
defs.def:ricot-weights:
For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.
\]
This is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), agrees with that density at source training atoms, and is positive and measurable at held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.
defs.def:spliced-estimator:
Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=
\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)
+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.
\]
Every displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), not as an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\). The regression and calibration dimensions are respectively \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\); only \(h\) is the boundary-splice bandwidth.
defs.def:regression-fit:
For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set
\[
\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},
\qquad
\widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.
\]
Using the same training indices with \(X_i\ge h\), let \(\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}\) be the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{J_{\mu,n}}\) of
\[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_i)^\top\beta\}^2+n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2.
\]
Define the untruncated fit
\[
\widehat\mu^{(-k)}_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h},&0\le x<h,\\
\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)^\top\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}},&h\le x\le1.
\end{cases}
\]
Empty local or interior samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridges and ordered bases make every fold fit unique. No clipping map or kink derivative is part of the construction.

assumptions.ass:known-propensity: \(e\) is fixed and known by the source-trial randomization protocol.
assumptions.ass:mean-transportability: \(\mathbb E_{F^T_{n,m}}[Y^T(d)\mid X^T=x]=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}[Y^S(d)\mid X=x]=\mu_d(x)\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).
assumptions.ass:residual-nondegeneracy: \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)\ge M^{-1}\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_S\)-almost every \(x\).

snapshot.stmt:
For fixed \((a,s,t,M)\) with \(s>1/2\), \(t>1/2\), and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence satisfying \(m/n\to\kappa\), the interval \(\mathcal I_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), with the finite zero-standard-error convention in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\), obeys
\[
\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\}\ge1-\gamma,
\]
and its maximal expected length is at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\). Uniformly over the class, the explicit four-term statistic \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}^2\), including the covariance between \(\widehat U^R_{i,h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat U^B_{i,h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), divided by the variance of the corresponding foldwise linear term converges in probability to one. The studentized linear term has Kolmogorov distance \(o(1)\) from \(N(0,1)\), and conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) the law of
\[
\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}|
\]
approximates its centered sampling analogue with error \(o(1)\). The threshold \(s>1/2\) gives the finite one-dimensional Hölder entropy integral, \(t>1/2\) controls the density-ratio calibration sieve, and the product relation controls the nuisance-product remainder. The conclusion includes \(a=1\), where the normal approximation is scaled by \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and the \(2M\) boundary-bias envelope remains explicit.

defs.def:bias-aware-interval:
Using only the displayed bias, multiplier-envelope, and standard-error statistics, define, when \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}>0\),
\[
\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\pm\operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}\!\left(\frac{\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}}{\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}}\right)\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right].
\]
If \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=0\), define
\[
\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-(\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}),\ \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+(\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})\right].
\]
This is the finite continuous extension of the bias-aware radius and is a singleton if both envelopes vanish.
defs.def:spliced-estimator:
Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define
\[

defs.def:bias-envelope:
For every \(h\in(0,1)\), define the observable fold-varying discrepancy
\[
C_{n,m}(h)=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=2C_{\mathrm{LP}}Mh^{s+1}+|C_{n,m}(h)|+2M\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)|.
\]
The middle term is required by the exact held-out interior decomposition; it is not generally equal to a calibration residual of one common fitted function. The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\).
defs.def:foldwise-inference-statistics:
For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define
\[
\widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_j^T),
\qquad
\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.
\]
